By the end of this video, you will understand exactly how this operation was built, how it is funded, and why, decades later, its funding is still going on. In 1971, Pakistan lost East Pakistan, which became Bangladesh. 93,000 soldiers surrendered in just 13 days. Zia ul Haq realized that conventional war is unwinnable, but by bleeding India with proxies, internal sabotage and internal pressure, they can win which came to be known as one cuts doctrine.

Punjab became the first testing ground. In the 1980s, ISI backed the Khalistan insurgency in Punjab to destabilize India, which led to years of violence. Also it triggered major events like Operation Bluestar but failed to break India's control over Punjab. In 1988 came operation to Tupac adopted from Afghani jihadi playbook. This time they went north, but Kashmir faced a problem Kashmiri Pandits existence and patriotism to India

where an obstacle to their mission. Pakistan. So a demographic shift was needed from 1980 to 1990. Anti pundit sentiment was instilled spreading hatred through Maulvi in mosques and Muslim gatherings. In 1986. Tensions rose when Ghulam Muhammad Shah announced the construction of a mosque on a historic Hindu

temple site, which Kashmiri Pandits opposed. Violence erupted against Hindus temples were desecrated, homes of pundits were looted and attacked. The country have gone and taken positions in mosques in the valley. This led to the first large scale exodus of Kashmiri Pandits. In 1990, 300,000 Kashmiri Pandits were forced to leave. Official records list 219 deaths and over 1200 unofficial deaths by 2004. Removing the pundits made it easier to portray Kashmir as a purely Muslim

political struggle against India. But this narrative didn't spread on its own. Behind the scenes operation, Tupac was taking a larger shape with backing from Washington and Afghanistan, bringing in money fighters and a missionary to keep it alive. From 1996 onward,

Afghan jihad veterans were redirected into Kashmir. They brought a key system to direct Washington's money. Let me explain this system to you. The US would send money to an Afghan businessman who was involved in Soviet jihad and often based in Dubai. The Afghani businessman would contact and Afghani broker and send him the money and receive a secret code in return. Then that businessman would privately contact the Pakistani ISI and share him the code.

Afghani broker would then contact a partner in Pakistan and share the transaction details and the code. Deci would go to the partner broker in Pakistan, provide the code and collect the money in local currency. The Afghani broker and the partner broker would keep records of the transaction and settle their balance later through future deal. This system is called Hawala Networks and this is how money was directed to Kashmir extremism right under the US nose.

In 1999, Indian Airlines Flight eight one for hijacking and Masood Azhar release became another turning point. Yeah yeah yeah yeah. For sure. Yes. In Salah Salah in Kabul again Salah. Around this period ISI took full operational control of Lashkar e Taiba and jaish-e-mohammed

sidelining the local militants during the same time. Musharraf, a convicted criminal by a Pakistani court, openly exposed being the biggest supporter of Lashkar e Taiba and stated he was liked by the militant group by early 2000. Indian politicians were meeting ISI linked handlers abroad with money reportedly flowing into elections, actively using the network and weapons being transported through political vehicles. By 2004 to 5 Pakistani funds were nerve reaching Indian journalists, politicians and clerics.

After the obligation of article 370, ISI reportedly told operatives to pose as Hindu supporters, joined BJP and worked secretly from inside. Because now Pakistan is starting to learn. religious leaders, and NGOs to support militant and influence related activities from late 20 tens to early 2020s, and estimated 450 crores is being covertly moved through Havana networks to fund influence campaigns. who subsequently became victims of targeted killings. With its Kashmir narrative struggling for wider acceptance, Pakistan leaned on Turkey and suddenly media platforms like TRT World and anadolu agency started broadcasting this report say many Pakistani and Indian Kashmiri journalists who have been hired by TRT world without credentials are pushing anti-India coverage. The same pattern appears in scholarship and political outrage. Turkey lures Kashmiri students with scholarships, only for some to be handed

to Pakistan backed network to push propaganda. Erdogan, Turkey's president, repeatedly drags Kashmir at UN to rally Muslims and back Pakistan's narrative. Despite India firm rejection, Turkey and Pakistanis officially co-hosted a UN event on combating hate speech to co-ordinate anti-India messaging under the cover of a neutral international platform. Turkey thought Pakistan a lesson that a narrative needs repetition to be effective. Truth is optional.

However getting a seat requires a recommendation letter controlled by Hurriyat leaders. Instead of helping the needy, these leaders sell the letters to wealthy families for 20 to 25 lakh, and that money is used to fund terror activities. Actively, this is the medical seat

pipeline that turns into a network of money and influence. ISI handlers guide students in Pakistan who bring cash back on vacation that is controlled by local terror networks. Between 2015 and 2018, 28 of 40 students who went to Pakistan on valid visas returned as trained terrorists, while another 100 never returned or disappeared, believed to be operating within terror groups in Pakistan occupied Kashmir.
